workbuddy.panel_reconcile: succeeded twice after the restart (job_state WORKING at 15:35:17Z and 15:37:17Z), i.e. the panel process can authenticate; before the restart the same call returned HTTP 401 AUTH_REQUIRED
workbuddy.defect_fixed: the session environment carried a stale gateway password (the first random one) while the running gateway is pinned; persisted the pinned value to the user environment so any future launch sees it

defects_found_this_round.finding: CODEBUDDY_GATEWAY_PASSWORD in the interactive environment was the gateway's first random password; the gateway on :8080 uses a later pinned one. The panel's escalation reconcile therefore failed HTTP 401 and the queue could never advance its in-flight job.
defects_found_this_round.fix: pinned value persisted to the user environment; verified GET /api/v1/health -> 200 and a real reconcile of job 859e3787.

defects_found_this_round.finding: A GUI started as a child of a tool call dies when that call returns -- verified with a DETACHED_PROCESS + CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB probe that wrote 'alive' and was then gone, and with Start-Process under PowerShell. The long-running panel must be launched as a long-lived task, not as a fire-and-forget child.
defects_found_this_round.fix: panel now runs as a persistent background task with the production interpreter and the credential in its environment.

defects_found_this_round.finding: The previous panel (pid 23268) had been running code from before the interpreter-resolution fix: it logged '[executor] MAA requested but unavailable (MAA_IMPORT_FAILED:ModuleNotFoundError)' while every other producer on the machine resolved the venv correctly. Its death at 23:19:40Z left learning/control_panel/latest.log truncated to 0 bytes and runtime_snapshot claiming AUTO_RUNNING with runtime_thread_alive=true -- an abrupt external termination, cause not identified.
defects_found_this_round.fix: restarted from the current tree; the failure line is gone and MAA capture is live.

unproven: Whether the old panel's abrupt death at 23:19:40Z has a cause that can recur (no crash report was written, so the crash path was not the one that ran).
